rejected.title: Creation stories and Country
card: Country is the land, waters, sky and living things that an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander group belongs to. It also includes the people's spiritual ties and duties to that place.
Creation stories tell how Country, people and law came to be. They are told through story, song, dance and art.
The Kulin Nations of the Melbourne region have stories of Bunjil, a creator who shaped the land and gave law to the people.
Creation stories also pass on knowledge, such as how to care for Country and how to live together. Each generation has learned them from Elders and passed them on.
rejected.remember: Creation stories carry knowledge of Country, people and law from one generation to the next.

a.q: What do creation stories such as the Bunjil stories pass on?
opts: How Country, people and law came to be
A list of the dates of past floods and droughts
The rules of trade with other countries
Written records kept by early settlers
a.why: Creation stories pass on knowledge of how Country, people and law came to be. They are not lists of dates or written records, because they are shared through story, song, dance and art.
a.clue: Think about what the stories explain about Country and the people.

b.q: An Elder of the Kulin Nations tells a group of children about Bunjil, and the children later dance the story. Why is this important for the knowledge in the story?
opts: It passes the knowledge to the next generation
It replaces the need to care for Country
It turns the story into a written document
It shows the story is only for entertainment
b.why: Telling and dancing the story is how each generation learns the knowledge about Country and law. It does not replace caring for Country, and the stories are not only entertainment, because they carry law and knowledge.
b.clue: Ask who learns the story and what they do with it.

version.title: Creation stories and Country
card: Country means the land, waters, sky and living things that an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander group is connected to. It also takes in the group's spiritual ties and duties to that place.
Creation stories tell how Country was shaped, how people came to be and where law comes from. Law here means the rules for how to live and how to care for Country.
The Kulin Nations of central Victoria tell of Bunjil, a creator ancestor who often takes the form of a wedge-tailed eagle. In their stories, Bunjil shaped the land and gave the people their law.
The stories are passed on through story, song, dance and art. Each group's stories belong to its own Country, and Elders still teach them to young people today.
version.remember: Creation stories are living knowledge of Country, people and law, carried in story, song, dance and art.

a.q: Which statement about creation stories, such as the Kulin Nations' stories of Bunjil, is correct?
opts: They explain how Country, people and law came to be
They are the same for every group across Australia
They belong to the past and are no longer taught
They are told only to entertain young children
a.why: Creation stories carry knowledge of how Country, people and law came to be. They are not the same everywhere, because each group's stories belong to its own Country, and Elders still teach them today.
a.clue: Think about what the stories teach, and whose they are.

b.q: A Year 8 class visits an art centre, where an Aboriginal artist is painting a creation story from her Country. What is the painting most likely doing?
opts: Passing on knowledge of Country and law through art
Inventing a new story to explain the shape of the land
Keeping a record of a story that is no longer told
Decorating the walls, as the story has no other use
b.why: Art is one of the ways creation stories pass on knowledge of Country and law, along with story, song and dance. The story is not new and not finished: it belongs to her Country and is still taught today.
b.clue: Think about how these stories reach each new generation.

a.best: They explain how Country, people and law came to be

b.best: Passing on knowledge of Country and law through art
